translations.answer: The original author found the `clear()` function in the `please_switch_` real-time branch and moved it to the non-realtime path. The maintainer confirmed that the `clear()` calls have been moved to the non-realtime path. There is no proof that a `clear()` call must be heap-allocated, and no commit was provided, so the reusability principle is to audit and isolate container lifecycle operations in the real-time path, rather than mechanically flagging all same-name calls as faults.
translations.applicability: Applies to old ros_control switch implementation and similar real-time container lifecycle audits.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is missing.
